subject: Post-call: FinServe private deployment connectivity & allowlist scheduling

Subject: Post-call recap & action items — private deployment connectivity

Alex — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on during the call: 

Summary of the call
- FinServe is evaluating a Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC + PrivateLink preferred) for low-latency access and data residency.
- Primary workloads: real-time transaction classification + embeddings for search; peak QPS ~120 r/s, typical 40 r/s.
- SLA/latency target: 95th <= 200ms for generation across billing hours.

Immediate asks / next steps (what we need from FinServe ops)
1) Egress IP allowlist: please confirm whether you want Redwood to provide static egress IPs for your NGFW allowlist, or whether you will set up PrivateLink and only allow the PrivateLink endpoint. We can support both; each has slightly different network config.
2) Preferred connectivity (PrivateLink vs VPC peering): you indicated PrivateLink is preferred but NetOps will confirm. If peering is required, we need VPC CIDR and peering window constraints.
3) Timeline for allowlist and firewall change — to schedule a staging run: proposed window Mon 2026-08-23 02:00–04:00 UTC (low traffic).
4) Contact for NetOps: netops@finserve.com (can you share the direct owner + contact info?).

I attached a short preflight template (redwood-privatedeploy-preflight-template.pdf) that lists ports, protocols, and sample NAT/egress entries. If you prefer, Marissa can run a quick readout with your NetOps team to walk the sheet.

Proposed owner sequencing on our side
- Jonas (sales) — timeline & procurement coordination
- Marissa (solutions eng) — technical runbook & cutover
- Karthik (deploy lead) — provisioning and final verification

Please reply with: 1) NetOps point of contact and preferred connectivity option, 2) whether you can confirm the proposed staging window or suggest alternatives.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0126

Thanks Jonas — good summary. A few answers inline and an ask for clarification from your network team.

Answers from FinServe
- Preferred connectivity: PrivateLink would be ideal because it avoids peering and we can avoid exposing egress IPs to our perimeter.
- NetOps owner: Diana Lee (cc'd) will own the firewall changes and scheduling; general NetOps inbox is netops@finserve.com.
- Staging window: the proposed Mon 2026-08-23 02:00–04:00 UTC works for us, pending a short technical alignment call.

NetOps clarification (Diana)
- If we go PrivateLink, what exactly does Redwood need from us for endpoint creation? We will need a list of expected source IPs for the PrivateLink (if any), TLS fingerpints, and which ports will be initiated from our side.
- We also need a draft of the egress IP set in case we need a fallback peering path; could you provide a provisional list for planning?

Also attaching our internal network owner info and preferred maintenance blackout windows.

Thanks — Alex

Hi Diana / Alex — quick technical clarifications from the solutions-eng side so NetOps can size the firewall policy: 

PrivateLink specifics (what we will need from you)
- We will create an AWS PrivateLink service backed by Redwood's private fleet in us-east-1. For endpoint creation we need: your endpoint subnet (CIDR), security-group rules for the endpoint, and a VPC endpoint owner account id for the enablement form.
- Traffic direction: FinServe will initiate TLS connections to the PrivateLink endpoint on port 443. No inbound connections initiated by Redwood required.

Fallback / peering approach (if you need it)
- If you prefer peering fallback, Redwood can provide a short-lived egress IP range for allowlisting during staging: the attached finserve-egress-ips-draft.csv is a provisional set (will be stable for the staging window).
- Ports TCP 443, TCP 80 (health) and UDP 53 (optional, DNS) should be allowed for the staging run. We will provide a signed BIOS cert thumbprint for the endpoint during the cutover.

Cutover verification plan
1) NetOps creates endpoint or applies allowlist per the template.
2) Redwood performs connectivity test from our staging fleet and shares logs.
3) We run a small traffic ramp (10% of expected QPS) and run latency/throughput smoke tests.

I'll be available for a 30-minute technical alignment call on Thu 2026-08-19 14:00–14:30 EDT if that works for you.

Let us know the endpoint subnet and the account id and we will draft the endpoint request form.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
